platform_policy_not_store_policy.definition: Fail if the user asks about a specific store's policy (return window, shipping, restocking fee, refund) and the reply attributes the rule to Cartwheel, the platform, instead of naming the store's policy. Pass if the reply names the store's policy, for example the store's own return window.
platform_policy_not_store_policy.boundary: The check is whether the reply names the store or the Cartwheel platform as the source of the rule. Not about citing a policy id (RESP-1). Not a fail when the user asks about the Cartwheel-wide policy itself. Not a fail when the store follows the platform rule and the reply still names the store.
platform_policy_not_store_policy.likely_evaluator: Code check: does the reply name Cartwheel as the source of the rule? Plus an LLM judge for whether the user asked about a specific store.
platform_policy_not_store_policy.requirement_source: Gap: SPEC.md has no requirement to check the store policy first. The rule exists in the policy doc cw-store-overrides and facts.yaml (store_over_platform).
platform_policy_not_store_policy.open_question: Two close negatives (004, 218); a third is still needed. Batch 4 may find one, otherwise record it as a data limit.

tool_lookup_mismatch.definition: Fail if the reply states a value (for example a price) that differs from what the tool lookup returned.
example_quotes: behaved correctly but the lookup showed a different cost than what they told the user
tool_lookup_mismatch.boundary: Not about invalid data the reply repeats (negative_price_presented_as_valid). The reply value must differ from the tool result.
tool_lookup_mismatch.likely_evaluator: Code check: compare the value in the reply with the tool result

write_without_enough_context.definition: Fail if the agent calls a write tool (issue_refund or cancel_order) without enough context to make a good decision about it: the user only asked how it works, it is unclear which item they meant, or something it needed (such as the reason) was never asked. Confirming with the user is not always required.
write_without_enough_context.boundary: Not about wrongly reporting success (RESP-2): the action itself should not have happened yet. Not a fail if the request was explicit and the agent had what it needed.
write_without_enough_context.likely_evaluator: LLM judge (it needs the user's intent), with a code check for a write call
write_without_enough_context.requirement_source: Gap: SPEC.md has no requirement to confirm before a write action.

user_role_not_used_in_reply.definition: Draft: the reply does not use the role of the user (shopper, merchant or support) when building the response, for example asking a shopper about another account. The cause may be in the loaded prompt or context.
user_role_not_used_in_reply.likely_evaluator: LLM judge with the caller role as an input
user_role_not_used_in_reply.requirement_source: Gap: SPEC.md does not say how the reply should depend on the caller role (to decide)

reply_reveals_inaccessible_order_info.definition: Draft: when a tool refuses because an order is outside the caller's access, the reply gives away something about the order or its owner (for example saying "your own orders", which hints the order is someone else's).
reply_reveals_inaccessible_order_info.boundary: Draft. Not about the refusal itself; the agent should still explain it (RESP-4).
reply_reveals_inaccessible_order_info.requirement_source: RESP-4 (explain refusals without revealing inaccessible order or user information)
example_quotes: should not have said "your own orders"

right_lookup_tool_not_used.definition: Fail if the user's request could be answered or verified with the right lookup tool and the agent does not use it well: it asks the user for information a lookup would find, skips the check, concludes there is no matching order without resolving the records (for example using list_my_orders when the user named a product, instead of find_order), or picks one of several matches without confirming which the user means.
right_lookup_tool_not_used.boundary: Not a fail if the right tool was called and returned nothing or an error (a tool or spec problem). Not about write actions (write_without_enough_context). Not about which policy is cited (platform_policy_not_store_policy).
right_lookup_tool_not_used.likely_evaluator: Code check on which tools were called and how many matches came back, plus an LLM judge for whether a better lookup was available and whether the agent confirmed among several matches
right_lookup_tool_not_used.requirement_source: Gap: SPEC.md lists TOOL-5 list_my_orders and TOOL-6 find_order but not when to use each. Revision to record: when the user names a product, use find_order first; when it returns several matches, confirm which one.

wrong_human_handoff.definition: Fail if the request is sent to the wrong place: the agent tells a support-role caller to contact support, or that a support agent will review it, instead of handling it or escalating; or it handles a dispute or a request it cannot resolve itself instead of escalating to a human (ESC-3).
wrong_human_handoff.boundary: Not a fail when a support caller is escalated to a human such as a manager through escalate_to_human. Not a fail when a shopper is told a human will follow up on an above-threshold refund (ESC-1). Not about what a support caller is permitted to see (a spec or tool question).
wrong_human_handoff.likely_evaluator: LLM judge, with a code check for a missing escalate_to_human call
wrong_human_handoff.requirement_source: ESC-3 (disputes and requests the agent cannot resolve); Gap for the support-caller case (RESP-9 in the draft SPEC revisions)
wrong_human_handoff.open_question: 051 (a shopper told a support agent will review) and 180 (a support role wanting more privileges to view account information) are not members yet: the user decides whether either fits the definition.

reply_not_direct_or_actionable.definition: Fail if the reply does not respond directly to what the user asked, or leaves them without the context and information they need for the next step (for example it lists unrelated items or orders, asks for something it could have looked up, answers from the wrong source, or gives no next step).
reply_not_direct_or_actionable.boundary: Not a fail when the reply answers the request and the next step is clear, even if the answer is no. Judged on the reply itself: the cause may also be another mode (lookup, policy), and a trace can be present for both.
reply_not_direct_or_actionable.likely_evaluator: LLM judge, plus a code check for a negative price in a tool result that the reply repeats
reply_not_direct_or_actionable.requirement_source: RESP-5 (direct language that explains the relevant decision); RESP-3 for invalid values
